Yukon Is a Dual-Loft Tiny Home That Feels Like a Cozy Retreat on Wheels for Four
27 photos
Photo: Amberwood Tiny Homes
Tiny houses are not a mainstream housing option just yet, but they are certainly attracting more attention from people seeking more affordable, sustainable, and minimalist ways to live. Rising property prices and a growing desire for more freedom, both personal and financial, have made compact homes an appealing alternative to traditional housing.
As interest in tiny homes continues to rise, manufacturers feel motivated to come up with increasingly versatile designs that offer comfort, style, and practical features. Today, tiny houses come in all shapes and sizes, but two-loft models that maximize vertical space and create separate sleeping and storage zones while keeping the main floor open for daily living remain among the most flexible designs.
The Yukon tiny house on wheels perfectly exemplifies this flexibility. With its traditional layout that keeps the common, social areas downstairs and puts the sleeping areas at loft level at opposing ends of the house, this model can adapt to different needs and lifestyles, accommodating couples, roommates, hosts, and even families.
This tiny home is designed and built by Amberwood Tiny Homes, a Canadian manufacturer based in Bow Island, Alberta. Part of the Hiebert Group, the company operates under its current name since spring 2025, but it has actually been in business since 2022. It offers several types of compact dwellings, including tiny homes on wheels, foundation-built tiny homes, and park model homes , each designed to offer quality, comfort, and year-round livability.
Photo: Amberwood Tiny Homes Described as a modern farmhouse-style tiny house, the Yukon combines the classic dual-loft layout with practical amenities and eye-pleasing aesthetics. It is perched on a triple-axle trailer and measures 28 feet (8.5 meters) long and 8 feet (2.4 meters) wide, which means it stays within legal dimensions for road transportation without special permits.
Its design is rooted in minimalism, but the included amenities and easy-to-navigate configuration make it just as comfortable and practical as a full-size home. The first thing that showcases this home’s mix of simplicity and elegance is the exterior, which is clad in white vertical board-and-batten siding, complemented by a roof design that adds some architectural character.
A central sloped roof is flanked by two elevated, flat-roofed sections, and the entire surface is finished in black standing-seam metal. Black-framed windows dot the facades, and a blue entry door adds a splash of color.
Yukon’s interior boasts a modern, minimalist, and functional design , with a calm, coastal-farmhouse aesthetic that pairs clean lines with a beautiful palette of white, warm wood tones, muted gray, deep navy blue, and earthy neutrals. The white shiplap walls, a vaulted ceiling in the center of the house, and multiple windows keep the space open and bright, while premium finishes, like natural wood planks on the ceilings, quartz countertops, and luxury vinyl flooring throughout, ensure beauty, durability, and low maintenance.
Photo: Amberwood Tiny Homes With a footprint of just 362 square feet (33.6 square meters), the interior is compact, but the open, linear layout makes good use of the available space, creating a nice habitat that can accommodate up to four people. Comprising an inviting living room, a full kitchen, a dedicated dining area, and two opposing lofts, it truly makes the most of its compact dimensions. What’s more, the full kitchen and bathroom, modern appliances, washer/dryer combo, and four-season design make it feel like a true home.
One of the things that the Yukon does differently from other tiny houses is the access to the lofts. The stairs leading to the main sleeping loft are positioned toward the rear of the house rather than taking up valuable space in the middle of the home. This arrangement leaves space for an open central living area and makes the interior feel more comfortable by improving circulation between the essential zones.
Made from beautiful stained wood, the staircase is also a statement piece. Instead of traditional spindles, it features a solid panel balustrade, and its space-saving L-shaped design makes it easy to climb. In addition, it serves as extra storage space, with the lower steps hiding handy drawers and the underside configured with open shelves. Snug yet open and welcoming, the living room is fitted with a full-size sofa, offering a comfortable place to relax. The adjacent full kitchen is designed with full-time living in mind, featuring all the essentials for everyday meals.
Photo: Amberwood Tiny Homes It’s really stylish, too, with navy blue lower cabinets and white upper cabinetry, complemented by gray solid surface countertops and stainless-steel appliances. A deep sink, four-burner cooktop, oven, range hood, and full-size fridge make it entirely modern in terms of functionality.
Another aspect that makes this home more livable than other models of the same size is the inclusion of a dedicated dining space. While many tiny houses rely on a basic breakfast bar or a counter extension for dining, the Yukon features a comfortable dining area for four people with an elegant round table, a built-in bench, and additional chairs that match the lounge sofa.
The dual-loft configuration offers flexibility in terms of sleeping arrangements, with both elevated areas luminous and spacious enough to accommodate double mattresses. If you don’t need extra sleeping capacity, one of the lofts can even be configured as a workspace, extra lounge, reading corner, or used for storage.
Photo: Amberwood Tiny Homes As for Yukon’s bathroom, it is just as functional as the rest of the house, with a vanity, a toilet, a walk-in shower, and some open cubbies for linen and toiletries. In the hallway, there is even a dedicated space for a washer and dryer, along with a full-height closet.
As mentioned, this is a tiny home that you can live in permanently, with quality insulation, in-floor heating, air conditioning, LED lighting, and many of the conveniences you would expect in a conventional home. For utilities, it comes with RV hookups, and like all the models in Amberwood’s lineup, the Yukon can be converted into a permanent foundation build if you’d rather place it in a fixed location.
The Yukon tiny house on wheels is listed at CAD$156,726 (USD $109,567) plus taxes, and the company delivers anywhere in Canada or the United States.
